problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+3y+4z=-6 \\  & y+z=-1 \\  & z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+18z=380 \\  & y+9z=190 \\  & z=19\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 18 & 380 \\ 0 & 1 & 9 & 190 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 19\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form.

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 18 & 380 \\ 0 & 1 & 9 & 190 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 19\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-9){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 18 & 380 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 19 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 19\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-18){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 38 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 19 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 19\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 76 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 19 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 19\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
